title: Traffic Governor Lab Journal: latency-cost-reliability experiments
content:
Purpose:
Quick lab notebook for interactive experiments and heuristics for the Traffic Governor — how to score and pick routes across regions and model variants balancing latency, cost, and reliability. This is intentionally informal: rough math, sketches, and open questions.

Goals
- Produce a simple yet explainable scoring function suitable for control-plane use.
- Define hysteresis and recovery rules to avoid oscillation during transient failures.
- Generate a decision tree that can be implemented in the routing DSL and tested in canary.

Constraints and assumptions
- Metrics available per candidate: p95_latency_ms, cost_per_token_usd, recent_error_rate (30m), capacity_util (%), model_compatibility_score (0-1).
- Hard SLO: 1200ms p95 for interactive product routes. Soft budget target: reduce per-token cost by 15% vs baseline.
- Short windows for reactions: 30s for fast failover, 5m for re-eval.

Scoring sketch (work-in-progress)
score = w_lat * latency_score + w_rel * reliability_score + w_cost * cost_score - penalty_if_incompatible
Where: latency_score = max(0, 1 - p95_ms / target_ms) clipped to [0,1]
reliability_score = max(0, 1 - error_rate / error_budget) clipped
cost_score = 1 - normalized_cost (lower cost -> higher score)
Weights baseline: w_lat=0.5, w_rel=0.35, w_cost=0.15 (tunable by route).

Decision tree (ASCII)
Root: is model_compatibility >= 0.8?
  Y -> compute score across candidates -> pick highest if score > threshold
  N -> prefer compatible fallback (compat >= 0.5) even if higher latency, unless reliability below min
If top_score < route_min_score -> trigger failover to safety-model-pool (dedicated low-latency small model)

Hysteresis and cooldown rules
- When switching away from a candidate due to error spike, mark it as quarantined for QC_COOLDOWN = 3min.
- If switching due to latency, allow re-eval after 30s but only migrate 10% traffic back to test.
- Track consecutive successful probes before full traffic resumption (successes_required = 5 within 10m).

Experiment setups run so far
1) 2026-01-12: Weight sweep (w_lat 0.2->0.8). Synthetic traffic with two-region latency skew. Result: higher w_lat reduced tail breaches but increased cost by 8%.
2) 2026-01-27: Compatibility penalty introduced (-0.6 if compat < 0.6). Observed fewer semantic errors in-app tests but slightly higher p95.
3) 2026-02-18: Hysteresis cooldown increased to 3m from 1m — reduced oscillation in failure-injection tests.

Observed trade-offs (notes)
- Aggressive cost favoring (w_cost >= 0.4) sends traffic to cheaper regional variants that have 10–20% higher p95; user-perceived latency regressions start to appear non-linearly above 12% p95 increase.
- Reliability penalties should asymmetrically outweigh cost incentives; a 1% spike in error_rate must drop score more than a 10% cost saving can compensate.

Open questions / decisions to make
- Thresholds: should route_min_score be absolute (same across routes) or route-specific? Recommendation: route-specific with a conservative global minimum.
- Should we incorporate model-quality signals (nlg_score/regressions) into the score? Feels necessary for content-sensitive routes.
- How to represent multi-objective tradeoffs in rollout UIs so non-engineering PMs can reason about expected impact?

Short TODOs
- [ ] Wire up model_quality signal (Ravi) — jira JIRA-PLAT-812.
- [ ] Run A/B with w_lat=0.6,w_rel=0.3,w_cost=0.1 on internal traffic for 72h. (Miguel)
- [ ] Convert ASCII decision tree into routing-DSL example and small unit tests. (Claire)

Quick replication notes
- Simulation harness: traffic-governor/sim (local). Use seed=42 for deterministic runs. Stress scenarios: region_outage, slow_cold_kv_cache, model_slowdown_by_1.5x.
- Logs: include per-decision explainable vector in the request trace (score breakdown) — very useful for postmortem.

Final thought (high level)
Keep the control-plane decision logic simple enough to audit and reason about. Complex ML-based routers can live in offline scoring/suggestions (Optimize team), but the control-plane should use transparent heuristics and enforce safety minima.

Notes to self: add quick chart of score distributions next session, capture user impact thresholds from product (what p95 delta is acceptable).
